parsed.title: Down-degree homomesy conjecture for trapezoid posets
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathscr T(a,b)$ be the trapezoid poset, let $J(\mathscr T(a,b))$ be its set of order ideals, and let $\operatorname{ddeg}$ denote the down-degree statistic. A probability distribution $\mu$ on $J(\mathscr T(a,b))$ is **toggle on antichains-symmetric** if, for every antichain $A$ of $\mathscr T(a,b)$, the expectation of the antichain-toggleability statistic satisfies

$$
\mathbb E[\mu;\mathcal T_A]=0.
$$

**Down-degree homomesy conjecture.** For every toggle on antichains-symmetric distribution $\mu$ on $J(\mathscr T(a,b))$,

$$
\mathbb E[\mu;\operatorname{ddeg}]=\frac{ab}{a+b}.
$$

This weakens the corresponding statement for rectangles because not every toggle-symmetric distribution on trapezoid-poset ideals has the same expected down-degree. In particular, it predicts the stated constant for the distributions arising uniformly from rowmotion orbits, but the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

parsed.title: The extremal root path conjecture for Schur σ-groups
parsed.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be a finite non-abelian $p$-group. Its root path in the descendant tree of $G/G^{\prime}$ is obtained by iterated quotients by the last non-trivial terms of the lower central series. For a parent $W$, the nuclear rank $\nu(W)$ determines the possible step sizes of edges leaving $W$. In the descendant tree $\mathcal{T}(C_3\times C_3)$ of the abelian $3$-group $C_3\times C_3$, let

$$
G=\operatorname{Gal}(\mathrm{F}_3^\infty(K)/K)
$$

be the Galois group of the $3$-class field tower of an imaginary quadratic field $K$ with elementary $3$-class group $\operatorname{Cl}_3(K)\simeq C_3\times C_3$, and let $c=\operatorname{cl}(G)$.

**Extremal root path conjecture.** The root path $(\pi^{i-1}(G)\to\pi^i(G))_{1\leq i\leq c-2}$ consists of edges of maximal step size, equal to the nuclear rank: for every $1\leq i\leq c-2$,

$$
\pi^{i-1}(G)\to\pi^i(G)\text{ is an edge of step size }s_i=\nu(\pi^i(G)).
$$

Here $3\leq c<\infty$ is the nilpotency class of $G$. The conjecture asserts that the tower group's path through the descendant tree is extremal at every stage; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

parsed.title: Simon's conjecture on extendable shellability of uniform matroid independence complexes
parsed.statement:
For integers $1<k\le n$, let $U_{n,k}$ be the uniform matroid and let its independence complex be the simplicial complex whose facets are the bases of $U_{n,k}$. A partial shelling is an ordering $B_1<\dots<B_s$ of bases that shells the subcomplex generated by those bases. **Simon's conjecture.** For every $1<k\le n$, every such partial shelling can be extended: if $B_1<\dots<B_s$ shells $\langle B_1,\dots,B_s\rangle$, then the remaining bases can be ordered as $B'_1<\dots<B'_t$ so that 
$$
B_1<\dots<B_s<B'_1<\dots<B'_t
$$
 is a shelling order of the independence complex of $U_{n,k}$. The source explains that this conjecture is widely believed to be false, notes counterexamples to extendable shellability for other matroid independence complexes, and says that proving or disproving it appears to require a genuinely novel idea.

parsed.statement:
Let $(\nu,\mu)$ be a pair of patterns of length four. For a permutation $\pi$, let $\operatorname{asc}(\pi)$ denote its number of ascents and let $\operatorname{last}(\pi)$ denote its last entry. For an inversion sequence $e$, let $\operatorname{dist}(e)$ denote the number of distinct positive entries and let $\operatorname{last}(e)$ denote its last entry. Let $I_n(\geq,-,>)$ be the inversion sequences avoiding the stated inversion-sequence pattern, and let $\mathcal{S}_n(\nu,\mu)$ be the permutations avoiding both patterns. **Lin–Kim's conjecture.** For every $n$ and each pair $(\nu,\mu)$ in

$$
\{(4231,3241),(4231,2431),(4231,3421),(2431,3241),(3421,2431),(3421,3241)\},
$$

$$
\sum_{\pi \in \mathcal{S}_n(\nu,\mu)}q^{\operatorname{asc}(\pi)}v^{\operatorname{last}(\pi)}=\sum_{e \in I_n(\geq,-,>)}q^{\operatorname{dist}(e)}v^{\operatorname{last}(e)+1}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a common bivariate generating-function equivalence between six permutation pattern-avoidance classes and the corresponding inversion-sequence class, refining the underlying enumeration by ascent and last-entry statistics. parsed.title: The product formula conjecture for pinnacle-set enumeration
parsed.statement:
For a finite set $S$ of pinnacle values, let

$$
q_n(S):=\sum_{I\subset S}2^{|I|}p_n(I).
$$

Write $S=\{s_1,\dots,s_p\}$ with $n\geq s_p$, define

$$
q'_n(S)=2^{n-1}2^{s_p-2}2^{-s_{p-1}}2^{s_{p-2}-2}2^{-s_{p-3}}\dots,
$$

and set

$$
D(S)=(d_1,\dots,d_{p-1}):=(s_1-1,s_2-s_1,\dots,s_{p-1}-s_{p-2}).
$$

Define abstract expressions by $E_1=x_{1,3}+x_{1,1}$, $E_{2k+1}=f_e(E_{2k})$, and $E_{2k}=f_o(E_{2k-1})$, where

$$
f_o(x_{a,k})=x_{a,k}\left(x_{a+1,\frac{k+1}{2}}+x_{a+1,\frac{k-1}{2}}\right),
$$

with $x_{a,0}=0$, and

$$
f_e(x_{a,k})=x_{a,k}(x_{a+1,2k+1}+x_{a+1,2k-1}).
$$

If $S$ has $p$ elements, define $r_n(S):=\operatorname{ev}(E_{p-1})$, where $\operatorname{ev}$ evaluates $x_{i,j}$ to $j^{d_{p-i}}$. **The conjectural product formula.** For all pinnacle sets $S$ and all $n\geq\max(S)$,

$$
q_n(S)=q'_n(S)r_n(S).
$$

This conjecture gives a general formula for the weighted enumeration $q_n(S)$ of permutations associated with pinnacle sets; the paper presents an algorithmic factorization and initial explicit cases, but no resolution is supplied here.

Let $\boldsymbol{P}=(\Omega,\preccurlyeq_{\boldsymbol{P}})$ be a poset, let $(H_i\mid i\in\Omega)$ be finite abelian groups, and let $\boldsymbol{H}=\prod_{i\in\Omega}H_i$. For a codeword $\beta\in\boldsymbol{H}$, define

$$
\operatorname{supp}(\beta)=\\{i\mid i\in\Omega,~\beta_{(i)}\neq1_{H_i}\\}
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{wt}_{\boldsymbol{P}}(\beta)=|\langle\operatorname{supp}(\beta)\rangle_{\boldsymbol{P}}|.
$$

Let $\mathcal{Q}(\boldsymbol{H},\boldsymbol{P})$ be the partition of $\boldsymbol{H}$ whose blocks are the sets of codewords having equal $\boldsymbol{P}$-weight. The poset $\boldsymbol{P}$ is **hierarchical** if $u\preccurlyeq_{\boldsymbol{P}}v$ whenever $u,v\in\Omega$ satisfy $\operatorname{len}(u)+1\leqslant\operatorname{len}(v)$.

**Fourier-reflexivity characterization.** If $|H_i|\geqslant2$ for all $i\in\Omega$ and $\mathcal{Q}(\boldsymbol{H},\boldsymbol{P})$ is Fourier-reflexive, then $\boldsymbol{P}$ is hierarchical.

This conjecture characterizes hierarchical posets through Fourier-reflexivity of their poset-weight partitions. The parser marks it as resolved; the supplied evidence indicates that the result was established in the source's cited literature, so it is recorded as solved.

Let $n>1$ be an integer, let $\zeta$ be a primitive $n$-th root of unity, and define the derangement set

$$
D(n):=\{\tau\in S_n:\tau(j)\ne j\text{ for all }j=1,\ldots,n\}.
$$

For a permutation $\tau$, let $\operatorname{sign}(\tau)$ denote its sign. **The root-of-unity derangement sum conjecture.**** If $n$ is even, then

$$
\sum_{\tau\in D(n)}\prod_{j=1}^n\frac1{1-\zeta^{j-\tau(j)}}=\frac{((n-1)!!)^2}{2^n}=\frac{n!}{4^n}\binom n{n/2}.
$$

If $n$ is odd, then

$$
\sum_{\tau\in D(n-1)}\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}\frac1{1-\zeta^{j-\tau(j)}}=\frac1n\left(\frac{n-1}{2}!\right)^2,
$$

$$
\sum_{\tau\in D(n-1)}\operatorname{sign}(\tau)\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}\frac1{1-\zeta^{j-\tau(j)}}=\frac{(-1)^{(n-1)/2}}n\left(\frac{n-1}{2}!\right)^2,
$$

and

$$

$$
|A+cB|_{delta} gtrsim_{alpha,beta,gamma} delta^{-epsilon}|A|.

parsed.title: The unchanged-symbol access conjecture for stable MDS convertible codes
parsed.statement:
Let $\lambda^{F}$, $k^{F}$, and $k^{I}=\lambda^{F}k^{F}$ describe the dimensions of a stable MDS $(n^{I},k^{I};n^{F},k^{F})$ convertible code, and let $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ denote the information-flow quantities for data downloaded from unchanged and changed symbols, respectively. **Unchanged-symbol access conjecture.** In the information flow model, for all stable MDS $(n^{I}, k^{I}=\lambda^{F}k^{F}; n^{F}, k^{F})$ convertible codes, one must have

$$
\lambda^{F}\beta_1 \geq (\lambda^{F}-1)\beta_2.
$$

This conjecture formalizes the intuition that creating new symbols for a final codeword requires removing interference from the other final codewords, which necessitates downloading sufficient data from unchanged symbols. It is presented as a lower bound motivated by prior access-cost results; its resolution is not specified here.

parsed.statement:

parsed.title: The 3-connected degree-swappability conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **degree-assignment** for $G$ assigns to each vertex $v$ a list $L(v)$ of colors with $|L(v)|=d_G(v)$, and two $L$-colorings are **$L$-equivalent** if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of Kempe changes. The graph $G$ is **degree-swappable** if, for every degree-assignment $L$, all $L$-colorings of $G$ are $L$-equivalent.

**Degree-swappability conjecture.** Every $3$-connected graph distinct from the complete graph and the triangular prism is degree-swappable.

This conjecture would strengthen the theorem that every $4$-connected graph distinct from the complete graph is degree-swappable. Earlier work gives examples of $2$-connected graphs that are not degree-swappable, so the conjecture concerns the boundary between these known negative and positive results.

parsed.title: Kempe-equivalence characterization of perfectly contractile graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ be a perfect graph. A **replication graph** $H$ of an induced subgraph of $G$ is obtained by replacing vertices of that induced subgraph by replicated vertices as defined in the paper. A **$k$-coloring** is a proper coloring using $k$ colors, and two $k$-colorings are **Kempe equivalent** if one can be obtained from the other by Kempe changes. The chromatic number of $H$ is denoted by $4\chi(H)4$.

**Kempe-equivalence conjecture.** The graph $G$ is perfectly contractile if and only if, for every replication graph $H$ of an arbitrary induced subgraph of $G$ and every $k \geq \chi(H)$, all $k$-colorings of $H$ are Kempe equivalent.

This would characterize perfectly contractile perfect graphs through the behavior of colorings of their replication graphs. The conjecture is presented as a new characterization, and the source gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

parsed.title: Intersection density conjectures for transitive permutation groups
parsed.statement:
Let $G\leq \operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a transitive permutation group. For $\omega\in\Omega$, write $G_\omega=\{g\in G:\omega^g=\omega\}$ and define the **intersection density** of $G$ by

$$
\rho(G)=\frac{1}{|G_\omega|}\max\{|\mathcal F|:\mathcal F\subseteq G\text{ is intersecting}\},
$$

where $\mathcal F$ is intersecting if for every $g,h\in\mathcal F$ there exists $\omega\in\Omega$ such that $\omega^g=\omega^h$.

**Intersection density conjectures.** (i) If $|\Omega|$ is a prime power, then $\rho(G)=1$. (ii) If $|\Omega|=2p$, where $p$ is an odd prime, then $1\leq\rho(G)\leq 2$. (iii) If $|\Omega|=pq$, where $p$ and $q$ are two odd primes, then $\rho(G)=1$.

These conjectures extend the Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem to transitive permutation groups and seek sharp restrictions on the size of intersecting families. The third assertion was disproved by constructing transitive groups of degree $pq$, with $p=(q^r-1)/(q-1)$, whose intersection density is $q$; consequently, the combined conjectural statement is refuted.

parsed.title: Longtime existence and convergence conjecture for discrete conformal curvature flows with surgery
parsed.statement: Let $(M,V,varepsilon)$ be a closed connected weighted marked surface, where $varepsilon:V\rightarrow\{0,1\}$. Consider an initial Euclidean or hyperbolic polyhedral metric induced by Glickenstein's discrete conformal structures on $(M,V,varepsilon)$, and allow surgeries by flipping whenever needed to maintain the weighted Delaunay condition. **Longtime existence and convergence conjecture.** The combinatorial Ricci flow and the combinatorial Calabi flow with surgery exist for all time and converge exponentially fast. This conjecture concerns the global behavior of the two principal combinatorial curvature flows for Glickenstein's discrete conformal structures. It is supported by results for some special cases, but the general assertion for arbitrary closed connected weighted marked surfaces remains open.

parsed.title: Pinheiro–Machado–Firer extension conjecture for partition-induced combinatorial metrics
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_2$ be the binary field and let $\mathbf{H}=\mathbb{F}_2^\Omega$. For $k\in[1,|\Omega|]$, write $\mathcal{P}(k,\Omega)$ for the covering of $\Omega$ by all $k$-element subsets, and let $\mathcal{CO}(\mathbf{H},\mathcal{P}(k,\Omega))$ be the partition by $\mathcal{P}(k,\Omega)$-weight. **Pinheiro–Machado–Firer conjecture.** For every additive code $C\leqslant\mathbf{H}$ and every $f\in\operatorname{Hom}(C,\mathbf{H})$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal{P}(k,\Omega)}(\alpha)=\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal{P}(k,\Omega)}(f(\alpha))\quad\text{for all }\alpha\in C,
$$

there exists $\varphi\in\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbf{H})$ such that $\varphi|_C=f$ and

$$
\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal{P}(k,\Omega)}(\alpha)=\operatorname{wt}_{\mathcal{P}(k,\Omega)}(\varphi(\alpha))\quad\text{for all }\alpha\in\mathbf{H}.
$$

Equivalently, for every $k\in[1,|\Omega|]$, the partition $\mathcal{CO}(\mathbf{H},\mathcal{P}(k,\Omega))$ satisfies the MacWilliams extension property (MEP). This conjecture concerns whether every weight-preserving homomorphism on an additive code extends to a global weight-preserving automorphism; its resolution is not supplied in the source.
